findings.claim: The service-definition doctor check can falsely pass a plist that does not actually launch prometheus-exec because it verifies raw text substrings instead of parsing ProgramArguments.
findings.evidence: Acceptance 4.2 requires doctors to verify the service definition; `inspect_service_definition` only checks `text.contains("prometheus-exec") || text.contains("daemon")` and extracts `Label` with `plist_string` via string splits, so comments or unrelated keys containing those words satisfy `service-definition` without proving the LaunchAgent executes `prometheus-exec daemon`.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse the plist with a plist parser or `plutil -extract`, validate the real `Label` and `ProgramArguments` array, and require the executable/arguments to match the configured prometheus-exec daemon invocation.

findings.claim: A rejected Wasm MCP request can leave uploaded code pinned in the artifact store because authorization happens after `put_pinned` and errors return without rollback.
findings.evidence: `build_request` stores code with `facade.artifacts().put_pinned(&code, &upload_pin)` before calling `ComponentAuthorizer::estate(...).authorization_for_bytes(&code)?`; if authorization fails, the function returns `Err` before `LocalExecutionFacade::submit` can transfer or release the upload pin.
findings.suggested_fix: Authorize Wasm bytes before pinning them, or wrap the post-pin validation path so every error releases the `upload:{request_id}` pin before returning.
